STUDY HALL COURSES:
Reporting On Politics 101
Reporting on local and national politics can feel opaque to those who have yet to crack the code. Perhaps more than even culture writing, politics requires knowledge of a specific, technical kind of language. In this
class
, Grace Byron will guide you on how to generate ideas, find outlets, and use the lingo that veteran politics reporters and editors use when building a story. From interviewing subjects, write-arounds, and opinion pieces, you will analyze a few pitches and stories to get a better sense of how to get started. You'll leave this one-hour class feeling prepared to start your political reporting journey and hopefully have a few ideas of how to get tips and pitch new editors.
Grace’s work has appeared in
The New Yorker,
Vogue
, and
The Nation
.
The 1.5 hour course will take place September 28th 10 AM PDT.
The standard price is $99. Study Hall members can use the discount code “
studyhallmember
” to bring the price to $49.50. For any questions, email
support@studyhall.xyz
.
Sign up

A Beginner’s Guide to Covering the Sex Industry
Sex work seems to be everywhere these days. Storylines about sex workers have popped up in shows like
Euphoria
,
Margo’s Got Money Troubles
, and
Hacks
. Yet even as OnlyFans has become a household name, few journalists actually understand the inner workings of this often underground industry — or how to build trust that’s needed to get sex worker sources to open up about these stories.
In this
course
, Lux Alptraum, an adult industry expert and one-time editor of the porn blog Fleshbot, will walk you through the basics of reporting on the sex industry. In addition to providing an overview of the different corners of the sex industry, she’ll also explain why so many sex workers do not trust journalists, and walk participants through the best practices for covering adult industry-related topics.
The 1.5 hour course will take place September 18th at 10 AM PDT/ 1 PM ET.
The standard price is $99. Study Hall members can use the discount code “studyhallmember” to bring the price to $49.50. For any questions, email
support@studyhall.xyz
.
Sign up
.
Interview with Wilbert L. Cooper
On the latest Study Hall podcast
episode
, Wilbert L. Cooper, a staff writer at The Marshall Project, discussed his new memoir
The Black Shield: An American Memoir of Family and Power
. In this conversation, Cooper also discussed the dynamic of reporting on criminal justice reform.
Changing A System From Within Ft. Wilbert L. Cooper
Podcast Episode · The Study Hall Podcast · August 24 · 39m
Apple Podcasts

Kim Kelly on labor reporting.
Katie Notopoulos on tech reporting.
Gaby Del Valle on covering the far-right.

submit

as a staff writer covering politics.

TIME
.

The Washington Post
.
Ashley Gold is joining
Semafor
as a tech correspondent.

OTHER RESOURCES
▶ Add to the Rate-Sharing Database
The
Freelance Solidarity Project
maintains an ongoing
Rate Sharing Database
to build a clearer picture of freelance pay—and, ultimately, change how we are paid. Add your rates, and help build a more equitable future for freelancers in the industry.
Press On
in collaboration with
IRE
is hosting a virtual Backgrounding Like a Boss workshop on Wednesday, September 16 at 12:00-1:30pm ET / 11:00am-12:30pm CT / 9:00-10:30am PT.
You can register for the training here
.
This workshop is an opportunity to learn the crucial investigative journalism skill of backgrounding. Backgrounding is an essential aspect of uncovering injustice and allows journalists and media makers to tailor their research, interview strategy, make sure they’re using properly attributed images & videos and verify whether information is factual. Participants will learn recommended protocols for deep backgrounding every source & study case studies of stories supported by advanced backgrounding techniques using free online tools.
Registration closes on September 9th so
please register early
.

for

.
STUDY HALL COURSES:
Reporting On Politics 101
Reporting on local and national politics can feel opaque to those who have yet to crack the code. Perhaps more than even culture writing, politics requires knowledge of a specific, technical kind of language. In this
class
, Grace Byron will guide you on how to generate ideas, find outlets, and use the lingo that veteran politics reporters and editors use when building a story. From interviewing subjects, write-arounds, and opinion pieces, you will analyze a few pitches and stories to get a better sense of how to get started. You'll leave this one-hour class feeling prepared to start your political reporting journey and hopefully have a few ideas of how to get tips and pitch new editors.
Grace’s work has appeared in
The New Yorker,
Vogue
, and
The Nation
.
The 1.5 hour course will take place September 28th 10 AM PDT.
The standard price is $99. Study Hall members can use the discount code “
studyhallmember
” to bring the price to $49.50. For any questions, email
support@studyhall.xyz
.

A Beginner’s Guide to Covering the Sex Industry
Sex work seems to be everywhere these days. Storylines about sex workers have popped up in shows like
Euphoria
,
Margo’s Got Money Troubles
, and
Hacks
. Yet even as OnlyFans has become a household name, few journalists actually understand the inner workings of this often underground industry — or how to build trust that’s needed to get sex worker sources to open up about these stories.
In this
course
, Lux Alptraum, an adult industry expert and one-time editor of the porn blog Fleshbot, will walk you through the basics of reporting on the sex industry. In addition to providing an overview of the different corners of the sex industry, she’ll also explain why so many sex workers do not trust journalists, and walk participants through the best practices for covering adult industry-related topics.
The 1.5 hour course will take place September 18th at 10 AM PDT/ 1 PM ET.
The standard price is $99. Study Hall members can use the discount code “studyhallmember” to bring the price to $49.50. For any questions, email

.

Interview With Astead Herndon

episode
, Astead Herndon, the editorial director of Vox and host of
America, Actually
, discussed how political media is evolving. Herndon talked about why traditional media fears new media figures like Hasan Piker, and how to step out of the partisan media bubble. In addition, he shared advice for reporters who want to cover politics.

'

Boston Magazine

Daniel Reale-Chin Wrote About His Personal Connection To Frank Ocean's Music
For
Xtra Magazine
and the 10-year anniversary of Frank Ocean's
Blonde
, Daniel Reale-Chin wrote about how his music was "tied" to Reale-Chin's "first queer loves." Reale-Chin wrote, "Ocean’s music helped me understand myself. It soundtracked two great loves in my life. But I’m in a new relationship now, one that I’ve built over many years. As for the music, Ocean’s songs don’t belong to anyone anymore. They’re beach songs, shower songs, driving songs. I’ve earned that."

For
Business Insider
,
Andrea Javor wrote an essay about her friendship with her "writing friend" who is 21 years her junior. mentor. Javor told
Study Hall
, "[she] is a mentor to me just as I am to her."
